claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, I need to gather some information about your situation. Let me begin with a few key questions.

**First, could you tell me the name(s) of the child or children you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have one child, Alex, who is 17 and lives with you in the UK.

Before I can fully assess your eligibility, I need to check the specific rules. Let me read the official guidance on Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. I've reviewed the official guidance on Child Benefit eligibility.

Based on what you've told me, Alex is 17 years old. According to the rules, **normally you can qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training**.

To help me determine your eligibility for Alex, I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, this could include school, college, university, or an approved apprenticeship)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's doing his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for that information. Alex is in approved education (A-levels at sixth form college), which is very relevant to the eligibility rules.

I just need to confirm one more important detail to complete my assessment:

**Are you a British citizen or do you have the right to reside in the UK?** (This helps me verify your own eligibility to claim Child Benefit)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen and I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review the rules carefully:

According to the official guidance, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if:
- You're responsible for a child under 16, OR
- Your child is 16 or over and under 20, AND they stay in approved education or training

In your case:
- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex is in approved education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- You live in the UK
- You're a British citizen with the right to reside in the UK
- Alex lives with you (so you're responsible for them)

All of these conditions are met, which means you should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.
